problem: The final website pass still allowed uneven pricing CTA geometry, variable header height, empty section whitespace and portal visual models that could feel oversized or escape their cards at narrower widths.
root_cause: Functional and content parity were already covered, but the final responsive geometry contract was only partially encoded in CSS and regression tests.
decision: Lock card/CTA geometry, public header height, empty-shell suppression and portal visual containment at desktop, tablet and mobile breakpoints.
prevention: Pricing CTAs use a fixed row height and flex cards keep their CTA at the bottom.
The canonical public header has explicit desktop/tablet/mobile minimum heights.
Genuinely empty section shells do not reserve vertical space.
Portal model visuals are width-contained and progressively capped at 1180, 900 and 640 pixel breakpoints.
Responsive geometry is guarded by the website coherence regression test.
